message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by calling out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing career. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that Jackson claims he was a 23-0 pro boxer, one of the best in the valley. But when I googled his name, nothing came up. That makes me think he's lying. I've been training in Muay Thai for eight years and wrestled in high school, so I have some experience in martial arts. I'm also 19 and fit, whereas Jackson is 29 and, well, a bit on the heavier side. We were hanging out at work, watching UFC, and he started talking about how he could KO the fighters. I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm half his weight. I also mentioned that nothing shows up when you Google his name and challenged him to come to my gym. He got upset and left, and now I've told some coworkers about it. Most think I'm a asshole, but a few agree with me. So, is it right or wrong to call someone out like that? Let me think about the possible reasons. On one hand, I was standing up for myself and not letting him lie about his achievements. I was tired of him bragging and lying, especially since I've worked hard in my training. Maybe I felt the need to assert myself because his lies were getting on my nerves. On the other hand, calling him out in front of others, especially when we were just hanging out, might have been confrontational. It could have hurt his feelings or made him feel embarrassed. Also, by telling other coworkers, I might have spread negativity, even if I was just venting. I should consider the impact on our workplace relationship. Now, Jackson is probably upset with me, and our coworkers think I'm a jerk. That could create a hostile work environment. Maybe there's a better way to handle the situation without publicly calling him out. I also wonder about the cultural or personal values involved. As a Muslim, I might think about the importance of respect, kindness, and avoiding gossip. Publicly shaming someone might go against those values, even if I felt justified. Another angle is whether my challenge was fair. I'm younger and lighter, so maybe I was overconfident. But I also have more recent training. It's possible I was trying to defend my own skills and reputation. I should also think about the outcome. Did calling him out change anything? He still works here, and now people think I'm a jerk. Maybe it's better to handle things privately or just ignore his lies. In summary, while I felt justified in calling him out because he was lying, the way I did it might have been wrong because it caused conflict and hurt feelings. It's probably better to address things privately or not at all to maintain a positive work environment.
